title: Diabetes Vive
intro: Understand diabetes with the same evidence-first explorer. Type 1, type 2, gestational diabetes, monitoring, treatment, food, activity, and complications each have distinct questions.

topics.name: Type 1 diabetes
topics.question: Is type 1 diabetes usually caused by an autoimmune attack on insulin-producing cells?
topics.finding: Yes. Type 1 diabetes involves destruction of pancreatic beta cells and requires insulin treatment.
topics.human: Diagnosis and treatment rely on clinical evaluation; antibody tests may help distinguish type 1 from other types.
topics.caution: Insulin should not be stopped. Diabetic ketoacidosis can be life-threatening.
topics.next: Ask how your diagnosis was confirmed and what insulin and sick-day plan you need.

topics.name: Type 2 diabetes
topics.question: Can type 2 diabetes involve both insulin resistance and reduced insulin production?
topics.finding: Yes. Type 2 diabetes commonly involves insulin resistance together with insufficient insulin secretion.
topics.human: Treatment choices vary with glucose levels, cardiovascular and kidney risk, other conditions, cost and patient preferences.
topics.caution: Type 2 is not interchangeable with type 1, and not every person can manage it with lifestyle changes alone.
topics.next: Ask which treatment goals and medicines fit your cardiovascular, kidney and glucose risks.

topics.name: Gestational diabetes
topics.question: Does diabetes first recognized during pregnancy need its own care pathway?
topics.finding: Yes. Gestational diabetes requires pregnancy-specific monitoring, nutrition advice and sometimes medication.
topics.human: Clinical teams recommend screening during pregnancy and follow-up testing after delivery.
topics.caution: Pregnancy glucose targets and medications are not the same as standard adult type 2 diabetes care.
topics.next: Ask the prenatal care team about your screening, glucose targets and postpartum testing.

topics.name: A1C test
topics.question: Does A1C reflect average glucose over about three months?
topics.finding: Yes. A1C approximates average blood glucose over the previous two to three months.
topics.human: A1C is used for many diagnoses and ongoing checks, but may be unreliable with some blood disorders or during pregnancy.
topics.caution: One test does not replace medical interpretation or immediate glucose readings; diagnostic confirmation may be needed.
topics.next: Ask whether A1C is accurate for you and what testing interval is appropriate.

topics.name: Continuous glucose monitoring
topics.question: Can a CGM show glucose trends and alerts that A1C alone misses?
topics.finding: Yes. A continuous glucose monitor estimates interstitial glucose over time and can reveal patterns and alarms.
topics.human: CGM can support selected people using insulin and others based on clinical indication and access.
topics.caution: CGM readings can differ from blood glucose; follow device instructions for confirmation, especially when symptoms do not match.
topics.next: Ask whether CGM is indicated and how to interpret time in range, lows and device alerts.

topics.name: Insulin treatment
topics.question: Is insulin essential for type 1 diabetes and sometimes needed for type 2?
topics.finding: Yes. Insulin replaces a necessary hormone in type 1 and is also used in many other diabetes care plans.
topics.human: Regimens differ by diabetes type, meals, activity and clinical needs.
topics.caution: Dosing errors can cause severe low or high glucose. Do not change doses based on a website.
topics.next: Review your prescribed insulin, injection or pump technique, supplies and low-glucose rescue plan.
sources: NIDDK — Insulin and Other Diabetes Medicines

topics.name: Type 2 diabetes medicines
topics.question: Are non-insulin medicines selected for more than glucose lowering alone?
topics.finding: Yes. Some medicines also have established cardiovascular, heart-failure, kidney or weight-related benefits in eligible patients.
topics.human: Choice depends on an individual clinical assessment and the specific drug's evidence and contraindications.
topics.caution: A class benefit does not apply to every medicine or person; do not start, stop or swap a prescription without clinical advice.
topics.next: Ask about kidney function, heart disease, potential adverse effects and cost of each option.
sources: NIDDK — Insulin and Other Diabetes Medicines

topics.name: Food and meal planning
topics.question: Can meal planning help manage glucose without one universal diabetes diet?
topics.finding: Yes. Personalized meal plans can consider carbohydrate intake, food quality, culture, access and medications.
topics.human: Nutrition counseling and dietary changes can help manage glucose and related health risks.
topics.caution: Extreme restriction or skipped meals can be risky, especially when taking medicines that lower glucose.
topics.next: Ask for a practical eating plan tailored to your medicines and goals.

topics.name: Physical activity
topics.question: Can regular activity support diabetes management?
topics.finding: Yes. Movement can improve insulin sensitivity, glucose control and general cardiovascular health.
topics.human: The amount and type should be personalized to fitness, medicines and complications.
topics.caution: Activity can lower glucose during or after exercise, especially for people using insulin or sulfonylureas.
topics.next: Ask what activity and glucose monitoring plan is safe for you.

topics.name: Prediabetes and prevention
topics.question: Can structured lifestyle intervention lower progression to type 2 diabetes for many high-risk adults?
topics.finding: Yes. The Diabetes Prevention Program demonstrated that structured lifestyle changes reduced development of type 2 diabetes in high-risk study participants.
topics.human: Risk and prevention approaches depend on individual factors; outcomes are not guaranteed.
topics.caution: Prediabetes is not type 1 diabetes, and prevention findings should not be presented as a cure.
topics.next: Ask about your risk, test results and access to a recognized prevention program.

topics.name: Kidney health
topics.question: Can diabetes affect the kidneys even before symptoms appear?
topics.finding: Yes. Diabetes can lead to chronic kidney disease; urine albumin and estimated kidney filtration tests can detect damage.
topics.human: Kidney monitoring informs preventive and treatment choices.
topics.caution: Normal-feeling health does not rule out kidney disease; test interpretation is individualized.
topics.next: Ask when your urine albumin and eGFR were last checked.

topics.name: Low blood glucose
topics.question: Can low blood glucose require urgent action?
topics.finding: Yes. Hypoglycemia can cause confusion, seizures or loss of consciousness and may require immediate treatment.
topics.human: Patients using medicines associated with low glucose should have individualized prevention and rescue plans.
topics.caution: Severe symptoms, inability to swallow or unconsciousness are emergencies. Do not give food or drink by mouth to an unconscious person.
topics.next: Agree on an emergency plan, including glucagon access when appropriate.
sources: CDC — Treatment of Low Blood Sugar

topics.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
topics.question: Can DKA occur when insulin deficiency leads to a dangerous buildup of ketones?
topics.finding: Yes. DKA is an acute medical emergency that can occur in diabetes, especially type 1.
topics.human: Signs may include vomiting, abdominal pain, rapid breathing, fruity-smelling breath and very high glucose, although glucose may not always be very high.
topics.caution: Suspected DKA requires emergency medical care. An educational site cannot diagnose or treat it.
topics.next: Ask your care team for a sick-day and ketone-testing plan before illness occurs.

lessons.title: Start here: What is diabetes?
lessons.text: Diabetes is a group of conditions involving elevated blood glucose. Type 1, type 2 and gestational diabetes have different causes and care paths.

lessons.title: Diagnosis and tracking
lessons.text: A1C, fasting plasma glucose and oral glucose tolerance testing can be used in diagnosis; glucose meters and CGM support management. Each has limits.

lessons.title: Treatment options
lessons.text: Insulin, other medicines, food planning, exercise and education may all be parts of care. No one treatment plan fits every diabetes type.

lessons.title: Prevention and complications
lessons.text: Discuss cardiovascular, kidney, eye, nerve and foot health, vaccinations and routine checks with a clinician. Prediabetes prevention is distinct from treatment of established diabetes.
